_: mesh — an online sim hockey league site (NHL 25) plus a player portal. repo ~/i/mesh, github angelwingscomms/mesh. WHAT IS BEING BUILT public pages: home, standings, schedule, game page with recap, teams, team roster, player page, news. portal (one logged-in user owns exactly ONE skater): season/playoff/career stat splits, progression charts off dated attribute snapshots, milestones and awards, and profile edits (name, jersey, bio, headshot) that queue for admin approval instead of applying directly. admin dashboard: teams and roster moves, attribute editing (each save writes a dated snapshot), the approval queue, news publishing, and a CSV importer for NHL 25 sim exports. plus: docs telling a league admin exactly how to upload a stats file and trigger the database update. STACK — SvelteKit (experimental kit@next) + svelte 5 runes + tailwind v4 + cloudflare workers + D1 (binding DB) + R2 (binding R2). pnpm only, never npm or npx. node 22. HOUSE RULES — these are the user's global AGENTS.md and are not negotiable: - snake_case for every variable and function name. - db columns, request/response JSON keys and page-load return keys are SINGLE LETTERS (schema below). expand to readable labels only in markup. - stored enum values are single characters. st: 'r' pending, 's' success/approved, 'f' failed/rejected. game st: 's' scheduled, 'f' final. user r: 'u' user, 'a' admin. - svelte 5 runes only ($props $state $derived $effect $bindable). never `export let`. - NO COMMENTS in code. clean names and structure instead. the only exception is a comment explaining a non-obvious WHY. - no variables that are used once. - tailwind utility classes only. no inline style= attributes, no

scaffold.s:
create the sveltekit project IN PLACE in ~/i/mesh (the plan/ folder already lives there, which is why --no-dir-check is passed).

run exactly:

  cd ~/i/mesh && pnpm dlx sv create . --template minimal --types ts --no-dir-check --no-download-check --add prettier eslint vitest="usages:unit+component" playwright tailwindcss="plugins:none" sveltekit-adapter="adapter:cloudflare+cfTarget:workers" experimental="versions:kit+features:async,remoteFunctions,explicitEnvironmentVariables,handleRenderingErrors,forkPreloads" --install pnpm

if sv rejects one experimental feature name as unknown (kit has removed features before — handleRenderingErrors and forkPreloads are the likely ones), drop ONLY that name from the features list and rerun. if sv still fails, `plan mesh scaffold --block "sv create failed: <paste the error>"`.

then, in this order:

1. package.json scripts. the scaffold wires playwright into the test script; every gate in this plan runs `pnpm test` unattended, and playwright would try to download ~150MB of browsers and hang. set exactly:
     "test": "vitest run",
     "test:unit": "vitest",
   leave "build": "vite build" alone and never add `wrangler types` to it. keep the scaffold's "check", "format" and "lint" scripts as they are.

2. pnpm-workspace.yaml. it will contain an onlyBuiltDependencies / allowBuilds block. ADD a packages entry beside it, at the top level:
     packages:
       - '.'
   without it pnpm 11 aborts install on the first cloudflare build with "packages field missing or empty".

3. run `pnpm approve-builds --all` if pnpm reports blocked build scripts (esbuild, workerd, sharp).

4. create .prettierignore with exactly these four lines:
     plan/
     .svelte-kit/
     .wrangler/
     src/**/*.test.ts
   the last line matters: the tests in this repo are planner-owned and byte-compared, so prettier must never reformat them. also add "plan/**" to the ignores array in eslint.config.js.

5. append to .gitignore:
     .env
     .log
     .wrangler
     .dev.vars

6. git and github:
     git init && git add -A && git commit -m "initial setup" && gh repo create angelwingscomms/mesh --public --source=. --remote=origin --push

stats_lib.s:
totals and standings, the two aggregations the whole site is built on.

CREATE src/lib/stats.ts exporting exactly two functions.

`totals(rows)` takes an array of gs-shaped objects (any field may be missing) and returns an object with:
 gp   = rows.length
 gl a pm pim sog hit blk toi fow fol sv ga sa so = the sum of that field across rows, missing treated as 0
 pt   = gl + a
 sv_pct = sa ? sv / sa : 0
 gaa    = toi ? (ga * 3600) / toi : 0
every returned number is a number, never null or undefined, even for an empty array.

`standings(games)` takes rows shaped { h, a, hg, ag, ot, st } and returns one row per team that appears in a FINAL game (st === 'f'; anything else is skipped entirely), shaped exactly { t, gp, w, l, o, pt, gf, ga } with keys in that order. scoring:
 - the team with more goals gets w and 2 points.
 - the loser gets o and 1 point when ot is truthy ('o' overtime or 's' shootout), otherwise l and 0 points.
 - gf and ga accumulate goals for and against.
sort: pt desc, then w desc, then (gf - ga) desc, then t ascending as the final deterministic tiebreak. the last one is not cosmetic — without it two identical teams swap order between requests and the page flickers.

place the planner's test:

  cp plan/tests/src/lib/stats.test.ts.txt src/lib/stats.test.ts
stats_lib.t: bash plan/verify_tests.sh && grep -qF "export function totals" src/lib/stats.ts && grep -qF "export function standings" src/lib/stats.ts && pnpm test && pnpm check

chart_lib.s:
the chart maths. there is NO charting library in this project and you must not install one — the progression charts are hand-rolled svg, which is about forty lines and loads instantly.

CREATE src/lib/chart.ts exporting exactly two functions.

`scale_points(values, w, h)` maps a numeric series onto a w by h box and returns [x, y] pairs:
 - empty input returns [].
 - x is evenly spaced: i / (n - 1) * w, and exactly 0 when n === 1.
 - y is inverted so the largest value sits at the top: h - ((v - min) / (max - min)) * h.
 - when every value is equal (including a single point) y is h / 2 for all of them, because that division would be by zero.

`line_path(values, w, h)` returns an svg path string built from those points: 'M<x>,<y> L<x>,<y> ...', coordinates rounded to at most two decimals with no trailing zeros (String(Math.round(n * 100) / 100)), and '' for empty input.

place the planner's test:

  cp plan/tests/src/lib/chart.test.ts.txt src/lib/chart.test.ts
chart_lib.t: bash plan/verify_tests.sh && grep -qF "export function scale_points" src/lib/chart.ts && grep -qF "export function line_path" src/lib/chart.ts && ! grep -qE '"(chart\.js|apexcharts|d3|recharts|layerchart)"' package.json && pnpm test && pnpm check

csv_lib.s:
the csv parser and the column mapper. this is the heart of the stats import, and it is deliberately format-tolerant because nobody has pinned down exactly which headers the NHL 25 export emits.

CREATE src/lib/csv.ts exporting: parse_csv, norm_header, ALIASES, REQUIRED, auto_map, missing_fields, header_hash, parse_toi, map_rows.

`parse_csv(text)` -> string[][]. a real rfc4180 pass, not a split:
 - strip a leading BOM (\uFEFF).
 - a field is quoted only when its first character is '"'. inside a quoted field, '""' is a literal quote and raw commas and newlines are content.
 - quoted fields are returned literally; unquoted fields are trimmed.
 - handle both \r\n and \n. a trailing newline must not produce a final row of [''].
 - empty fields are preserved: 'a,,c' is ['a','','c'].

`norm_header(h)` -> lowercase, then '+' becomes 'plus', '-' becomes 'minus', '/' is dropped, then every remaining non-alphanumeric character is dropped. so '+/-' becomes 'plusminus' and ' Shots On Goal ' becomes 'shotsongoal'. the plus/minus rule exists because stripping punctuation first would flatten '+/-' to an empty string and it would match everything.

`ALIASES` maps each canonical field to its accepted normalised headers, in this order:
 player: ['player','name','playername','skater']
 team:   ['team','tm','club']
 date:   ['date','gamedate','gd']
 opp:    ['opp','opponent','vs','against']
 gl:     ['g','goals','gl']
 a:      ['a','assists','ast']
 pm:     ['plusminus','pm']
 pim:    ['pim','penaltyminutes']
 sog:    ['s','shots','sog','shotsongoal']
 hit:    ['hits','hit','hts']
 blk:    ['blk','blocks','blockedshots','bs']
 toi:    ['toi','timeonice']
 fow:    ['fow','faceoffswon','fw']
 fol:    ['fol','faceoffslost','fl']
 sv:     ['sv','saves']
 ga:     ['ga','goalsagainst']
 sa:     ['sa','shotsagainst']
 so:     ['so','shutout','shutouts']

`REQUIRED` = ['player','team','date','opp'].

`auto_map(headers)` -> { field: original header } for every field it can place. walk fields in ALIASES order, and for each take the first header whose norm_header value is in that field's alias list and that no earlier field already claimed. fields with no match are simply absent from the object.

`missing_fields(map)` -> the REQUIRED entries not present in the map, in REQUIRED order.

`header_hash(headers)` -> a stable id for a header set: normalise each header, sort, join with '|'. order and case must not change it. this is what lets a saved column preset be found again on the next upload; it is not a security hash and does not need to be one.

`parse_toi(v)` -> seconds. 'mm:ss' and 'hh:mm:ss' both work; a bare number is seconds; anything else, including '' and '-', is 0.

`map_rows(headers, rows, map)` -> one object per row keyed by canonical field:
 - player, team, date and opp stay strings.
 - toi goes through parse_toi.
 - every other mapped field becomes a number, with '' or unparseable becoming 0.
 - a row whose player value is empty after trimming is dropped entirely (export files end in blank or total rows).
 - fields absent from the map are absent from the object.

place the planner's test:

  cp plan/tests/src/lib/csv.test.ts.txt src/lib/csv.test.ts
csv_lib.t: bash plan/verify_tests.sh && grep -qF "export function parse_csv" src/lib/csv.ts && grep -qF "export function auto_map" src/lib/csv.ts && grep -qF "export function parse_toi" src/lib/csv.ts && pnpm test && pnpm check

approve_lib.s:
the whitelist that decides what a coach is allowed to change about their own player. this is a trust boundary: everything a user submits about their player passes through validate_edit before it is ever written, and the admin approval step calls apply_edit rather than writing the field itself.

CREATE src/lib/approve.ts exporting EDITABLE, validate_edit, apply_edit.

`EDITABLE` = ['n', 'j', 'b', 'h'] — name, jersey, bio, headshot key. nothing else is user-editable, ever: team, position, status and role are admin-only and must not appear in this list.

`validate_edit(f, v)` -> an error tag string, or null when the value is acceptable:
 - f not in EDITABLE -> 'field'
 - 'n': trimmed length must be 2..40 -> 'name'
 - 'j': must match /^\d{1,2}$/ and be 1..99 -> 'jersey'
 - 'b': length must be <= 800 -> 'bio'   (empty is fine)
 - 'h': must match /^h\/[a-z0-9-]+\.(jpg|png|webp)$/ -> 'headshot'. this is deliberately only keys we minted ourselves in R2, so a user cannot point their headshot at an external url or walk out of the prefix with '../'.

`apply_edit(player, f, v)` -> a NEW object (never mutate the argument), equal to player with f set to v, except 'j' which is stored as a number. it calls validate_edit first and throws `new Error(tag)` when that returns a tag.

place the planner's test:

  cp plan/tests/src/lib/approve.test.ts.txt src/lib/approve.test.ts
approve_lib.t: bash plan/verify_tests.sh && grep -qF "export const EDITABLE" src/lib/approve.ts && grep -qF "export function apply_edit" src/lib/approve.ts && pnpm test && pnpm check

attrs_lib.s:
the attribute vocabulary. the public player page, the portal progress charts and the admin ratings editor all read this one list, so key names, order and labels can never drift apart.

CREATE src/lib/attrs.ts:

export const ATTRS: [string, string][] = [
	['sk', 'skating'],
	['sh', 'shooting'],
	['pa', 'passing'],
	['ck', 'checking'],
	['df', 'defence'],
	['en', 'endurance'],
	['fo', 'faceoffs'],
	['iq', 'hockey iq']
];

it is a plain array of pairs rather than an object because order is meaningful and object key order is not something to rely on. attribute values are integers 0..99 and are stored as a JSON object keyed by the short code in at.v — adding a rating later means appending one pair here, and old snapshots simply lack that key, which every reader already treats as 0.

there is no test for this file: it is data with no behaviour, and the pages that consume it are gated on their own greps.
attrs_lib.t: grep -qF "export const ATTRS" src/lib/attrs.ts && grep -qF "'hockey iq'" src/lib/attrs.ts && pnpm test && pnpm check

home_page.s:
the landing page: what happened, what is next, who is hot.

CREATE src/routes/+page.server.ts. get `const db = platform!.env.DB` and `const se = await active_season(db)`; if there is no active season return every key as an empty array. otherwise return, all in one load:

 g: next 5 scheduled games —
    select g.i as i, g.dt as dt, ht.ab as h, at.ab as a from g join t ht on ht.i = g.h join t at on at.i = g.a where g.s = ? and g.st = 's' order by g.dt asc limit 5
 r: last 5 finals —
    same joins, with g.hg as hg, g.ag as ag, g.ot as ot, where g.st = 'f' order by g.dt desc limit 5
 n: latest 3 published posts —
    select i, ti, sl, pb from ns where pb is not null order by pb desc limit 3
 l: the top 10 scorers —
    select p.i as i, p.n as n, tm.ab as ab, sum(gs.gl) as gl, sum(gs.a) as a, sum(gs.gl) + sum(gs.a) as pt from gs join p on p.i = gs.pi join g on g.i = gs.gi left join t tm on tm.i = p.t where g.s = ? and g.st = 'f' group by p.i order by pt desc, gl desc limit 10

CREATE src/routes/+page.svelte — `let { data } = $props()`, four cards in a responsive grid (grid gap-6 md:grid-cols-2), each card bg-board border border-line rounded-[--radius-card] p-5:
 - "upcoming" — each row "<away ab> @ <home ab>" and the date via `new Date(dt).toLocaleDateString()`, linking to /game/<i>.
 - "recent results" — "<away ab> <ag> — <hg> <home ab>" plus " (ot)" when ot is truthy, linking to /game/<i>.
 - "league news" — title linking to /news/<sl>.
 - "points leaders" — a table of name (linking to /player/<i>), team ab, gl, a, pt.
every empty list renders a muted lowercase "nothing yet" line rather than an empty card.

/teams and /team/[ab] — the club index and the roster.

CREATE src/routes/teams/+page.server.ts — select i, n, ab, d from t order by d, n. return { t: rows }.

CREATE src/routes/teams/+page.svelte — a grid (grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3) of cards, each the team name (bold), its abbrev uppercased in the markup only, and its division, linking to /team/<ab>.

player_page.s: /player/[i] — the public card for one skater: who they are, what they have done, what they have won. CREATE src/routes/player/[i]/+page.server.ts: - the player joined to their team; `error(404, 'no such player')` when missing. - every stat line they have, with the game type and season attached: select gs.*, g.ty as ty, g.s as s from gs join g on g.i = gs.gi where gs.pi = ? and g.st = 'f' - build three splits with `totals()` from #lib/stats: regular season of the ACTIVE season (ty 'r' and s = active), playoffs of the active season (ty 'p'), and career (every row). return { p, t, s: { r, p: po, c }, w, at }. name the playoff key `p` inside `s` but keep the player under the top-level `p` — they are different objects at different depths, do not flatten them. - w: select n, ty, d from aw where p = ? order by d desc - at: the most recent attribute snapshot only — select v, d from at where p = ? order by d desc limit 1 — parsed with JSON.parse. CREATE src/routes/player/[i]/+page.svelte: - header: the headshot when p.h is set () else a bg-line placeholder circle holding the jersey number; then name as h1, and a muted line "# · · ". map ps to a label with a local record: c centre, l left wing, r right wing, d defence, g goalie. - a splits table: three rows (regular, playoffs, career) by gp, g, a, pts, +/-, pim, sog, hits, blk. when p.ps === 'g' show sv, ga, sa, sv% (toFixed(3)) and gaa (toFixed(2)) instead. - "attributes" — the latest snapshot as a simple two-column list using ATTRS from #lib/attrs for the labels and order; a muted "no ratings yet" when there is no snapshot. - "awards" — the aw rows, or a muted "none yet".

admin_roster.s:
/admin/roster — teams, players, roster moves and game results in one page. this is the deliverable's "roster moves, attribute edits, content publishing" dashboard minus ratings and news, which get their own pages.

CREATE src/routes/admin/roster/+page.server.ts. load returns { t: teams, p: players with their team abbrev, u: every user (i, e, n) for the link dropdown, g: the active season's games with both abbrevs, se }.

actions, each doing exactly one insert or update and returning nothing:
 `team_new`: n, ab (lowercased, trimmed), d -> insert into t. reject a duplicate ab with fail(400, { m: 'abbrev taken' }).
 `player_new`: n, ps, j, t (team id or '') -> insert into p with st 'a', u null, b ''.
 `player_move`: i, t -> update p set t = ? where i = ?. an empty t writes null, which is what free agency is.
 `player_edit`: i, j, ps, st -> update those three columns.
 `player_link`: i, u -> update p set u = ? where i = ?, after checking with `select i from p where u = ? and i != ?` that the user does not already own another player; fail(400, { m: 'that user already has a player' }) if they do. one user owns one skater — this check is the only thing enforcing it.
 `game_new`: h, a, dt (an <input type="date"> value, stored as Date.parse(v)), ty -> insert into g with st 's'.
 `game_result`: i, hg, ag, ot ('', 'o' or 's') -> update g set hg = ?, ag = ?, ot = ?, st = 'f'. this is what moves a game into the standings.
 `game_recap`: i, rc -> update g set rc = ?. plain text; paragraphs are blank-line separated.

CREATE src/routes/admin/roster/+page.svelte — four sections with lowercase headings: teams, players, games, and a recap editor. every text form uses `use:ctrlEnter={submit}`; the select-only forms (player_move, game_result) submit on change is NOT allowed — they get an explicit "save" button, because a mis-click must not reassign a player. use <input type="date"> for dates rather than any date picker.

expect this page to be long and plain. it is an admin tool: tables, selects, buttons, no styling beyond the tokens.

admin_attrs.s:
/admin/attrs — attribute editing, which is really snapshot writing. every save appends a dated row to at; nothing is ever updated in place, because the progression charts ARE the history and an in-place edit would erase it.

the attribute keys, their order and their labels come from ATTRS in src/lib/attrs.ts, which already exists. do not redefine that list here and do not hard-code a key anywhere on this page.

CREATE src/routes/admin/attrs/+page.server.ts:
 - load: every active player with team abbrev for the picker, plus, when `url.searchParams.get('p')` is set, that player and their snapshots newest first (select i, d, v, no from at where p = ? order by d desc).
 - action `snap`: read p, a note field, and one form value per ATTRS key. clamp each to an integer 0..99 (Number.isFinite, Math.round, Math.min/Math.max) and drop anything not in ATTRS — the form is user input even when the user is an admin. insert into at (i, p, d, v, no) with d = now() and v = JSON.stringify(the clamped object). never update or delete an existing at row.
 - action `award`: p, n, ty ('a' or 'm') -> insert into aw with d = now() and s = the active season id.

CREATE src/routes/admin/attrs/+page.svelte:
 - a player picker: a form with a <select name="p"> and a "load" button that GETs ?p=<id> (method="get").
 - when a player is loaded: one labelled <input type="number" min="0" max="99"> per ATTRS entry, prefilled from the latest snapshot, a note text input, and a "save snapshot" button. `use:ctrlEnter={submit}`.
 - the snapshot history below: date, note, and the values as a compact "sk 80 · sh 77 · ..." line so an admin can see the progression they are adding to.

CREATE src/routes/admin/approvals/+page.server.ts: - load: select pe.i as i, pe.f as f, pe.v as v, pe.c as c, p.i as pi, p.n as pn, u.e as ue from pe join p on p.i = pe.p join u on u.i = pe.u where pe.st = 'r' order by pe.c asc — oldest first, because a queue is a queue. also load the 20 most recently decided rows for an audit trail. - action `ok`: load the pe row and its player, then `const next = apply_edit(player, row.f, row.v)` from #lib/approve — do NOT write row.v into the column yourself; apply_edit is the tested code that validates and coerces, and a value can have gone stale or invalid between request and review. wrap it in try/catch and on a thrown tag mark the row 'f' with that tag as the reason and stop. on success: update p set n/j/b/h = the value from next for that field, then update pe set st = 's', rv = locals.user.i, rd = now(). - action `no`: update pe set st = 'f', rv, rd. no other write. admin_import.s:
/admin/import — the NHL 25 stats importer, and the reason #lib/csv exists. two phases, no server-side session state between them: phase one stores the file in R2 and hands the browser back a key plus a suggested column map; phase two reads that key back and commits.

CREATE src/routes/admin/import/+page.server.ts.

load: the 20 most recent im rows (newest first) with their status and error.

action `upload`:
 - read the file; fail(400, { m: 'choose a csv file' }) when missing, over 5 * 1024 * 1024 bytes, or its name does not end .csv.
 - `const rows = parse_csv(await file.text())`; fail(400, { m: 'that file has no rows' }) when rows.length < 2.
 - `const headers = rows[0]`, `const hs = header_hash(headers)`.
 - look for a saved preset: select v from mp where hs = ?. use JSON.parse(v) when found, otherwise `auto_map(headers)`.
 - store the raw file: `const k = 'im/' + uid() + '.csv'` into R2 with contentType 'text/csv'.
 - return { k, f: file.name, h: headers, m: the map, mi: missing_fields(map), pv: map_rows(headers, rows.slice(1, 6), map) }.

action `commit`:
 - read k, f and the map (one form field per canonical field, named by the field, whose value is the chosen header or '').
 - fail(400, { m: 'map the required columns' }) when missing_fields(map) is not empty. re-read the file from R2 by k and re-parse it — never trust rows posted back from a browser.
 - insert an im row with st 'r' up front, so a crash mid-import leaves a visible "running" record rather than silence.
 - `const data = map_rows(headers, rows.slice(1), map)`, then for each row, in one loop:
   * resolve the team by `lower(ab) = lower(?)` on the team column; unresolved -> skip the row and count it.
   * resolve the player by `lower(n) = lower(?)` on the player column, preferring one already on that team; unresolved -> skip and count.
   * resolve the game: same season, both team ids in (h, a), and dt inside the calendar day of the parsed date (Date.parse(date), floored to midnight utc, and dt < that + 86400000). when no game matches, CREATE one — insert into g with st 'f', ty 'r', h = the row's team when it is the home side (decide by whether the opponent column was seen as away first; when it is ambiguous, put the row's own team as home) and hg/ag null — and count it as created. without this a stats file for a game nobody entered by hand would import as zero rows, which is the failure mode that makes an importer useless.
   * upsert the stat line: insert into gs (...) values (...) on conflict (gi, pi) do update set every stat column to the excluded value. re-importing a corrected file must overwrite, not duplicate — that is what the unique(gi, pi) index is for.
 - after the loop, for every game touched whose hg/ag is still null, set hg/ag to the summed gl of each side's imported rows and st 'f'. this is right when the export lists every scorer and wrong when it does not, so the docs step must tell admins to check the score on the game page afterwards.
 - insert or replace the mp preset for this header hash so the next upload of the same export skips the mapping form entirely.
 - update the im row: st 's', n = the number of stat lines written; or st 'f' with er = the error message inside a catch. always leave a terminal status.
 - return { n, sk: skipped count, gc: games created }.

CREATE src/routes/admin/import/+page.svelte:
 - step 1: <form method="post" action="?/upload" enctype="multipart/form-data"> with a file input (accept=".csv") and an "upload" button.
 - step 2, shown only once form?.k exists: a hidden k and f, then one row per canonical field — the field's lowercase label, a <select name="<field>"> listing every header from form.h plus an empty "— none —" option with the suggested header preselected, and required fields marked with a lowercase "(required)". the preview table under it renders form.pv. the "import" button posts action="?/commit".
 - after a commit, a result line: "<n> stat lines imported, <sk> rows skipped, <gc> games created" and a reminder link to /admin/roster to check scores.
 - the import history table at the bottom.

do not stream, do not background this, do not add a queue. a sim export is a few hundred rows and a worker request handles it in one pass.

docs.s:
the documentation deliverable. two files, written for a league admin who is not a developer.

CREATE docs/imports.md — "uploading NHL 25 stats":
 - export the skater and goalie stats from the sim as CSV, one file per run.
 - required columns: player, team, date, opponent. everything else is optional but recognised: goals, assists, +/-, pim, shots, hits, blocks, toi, faceoffs won/lost, and for goalies saves, shots against, goals against, shutouts. list the accepted header spellings straight from ALIASES in src/lib/csv.ts.
 - dates must be a form Date.parse understands (2026-01-02 is safest). TOI must be mm:ss or hh:mm:ss — a bare number is read as SECONDS, so a column of decimal minutes will import wrong.
 - the exact click path: sign in as an admin, /admin/import, choose the file, upload, check the suggested column mapping, fix any dropdown marked required, check the five-row preview, press import.
 - what happens: teams and players are matched by name, case-insensitively; a game that does not exist yet is created and its score is guessed from the goals in the file, so CHECK the score on /admin/roster afterwards; re-uploading a corrected file for the same game overwrites those stat lines rather than duplicating them.
 - the mapping is remembered per column layout, so the second upload of the same export format needs no mapping at all.
 - troubleshooting: "rows skipped" means a player or team name did not match — fix the name in /admin/roster or in the file and re-upload; a failed import shows its error in the history table at the bottom of the page and on /admin.

CREATE README.md — what the project is, the stack, `pnpm install`, the .env keys and where google credentials come from (authorised redirect uris http://localhost:5173/google and the production /google), the local database commands from the preamble, the one-line sql that promotes the first admin, `pnpm test` / `pnpm check` / `pnpm build`, the deploy command, a link to docs/imports.md, and a short "launch week" section saying bugs go to github issues on angelwingscomms/mesh with the page url and what was expected.

deploy.s:
production on cloudflare workers. every wrangler command here needs the `env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` prefix — the exported token lacks the scopes and shadows the working OAuth login.

1. create the real resources and copy the returned uuid into the `database_id` field of wrangler.jsonc, replacing the "local" placeholder:
     env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN pnpm exec wrangler d1 create mesh
     env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN pnpm exec wrangler r2 bucket create mesh
2. migrate production:
     env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN pnpm exec wrangler d1 migrations apply mesh --remote
3. the two secrets, as per-worker secrets:
     env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN pnpm exec wrangler secret put GOOGLE_ID
     env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN pnpm exec wrangler secret put GOOGLE_SECRET
   these arrive on platform.env as plain strings, and get_secret already accepts both those and a secrets-store binding, so moving to a store later is a wrangler.jsonc change with no code change.
4. add the deployed origin's /google to the authorised redirect uris in the google cloud console. if you cannot reach that console, finish the deploy and then `plan mesh deploy --block "deployed, but the production /google redirect uri still needs adding in the google console"`.
5. deploy:
     env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN pnpm exec wrangler deploy
6. promote the first admin against production once a real account has signed in:
     env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN pnpm exec wrangler d1 execute mesh --remote --command "update u set r = 'a' where e = '<the admin email>'"

the gate deploys, pulls the deployed url out of wrangler's own output, and fetches the live homepage. if wrangler is not authenticated it will say so — run `env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN pnpm exec wrangler login`, or block if no browser is available.
deploy.t: env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN pnpm exec wrangler deploy > /tmp/mesh_deploy.log 2>&1 && grep -qF "workers.dev" /tmp/mesh_deploy.log && curl -sf "$(grep -oE 'https://[a-z0-9.-]+workers\.dev' /tmp/mesh_deploy.log | head -1)" | grep -qiF "standings"
